newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Fewer Swedes believe economy will worsen - poll.
newsitem.headline: Fewer Swedes believe economy will worsen - poll.

text.p: Some 20 percent of Swedes believe the economic situation will worsen compared to 24 percent in April and 38 percent in May one year ago, a poll by Statistics Sweden said on Monday.
Statistics Sweden, the country's main bureau of statistics, said this portrayed continued optimism about the Swedish economy.
Some 28 percent of Swedes in the survey said they believed the general economic situation would improve over the next 12 months compared to 30 percent in April and 19 percent one year ago.
The number of Swedes who believe the economy will improve fell by two percentage points in May, the poll showed.

Expectations for inflation were the same. Swedes surveyed said they expected consumer prices to rise 1.3 percent over the next year. This is unchanged from April and compares to 1.9 percent one year ago.
Fewer Swedes, or 37 percent, believe unemployment will increase over the next 12 months. This compares to 40 percent in April and 49 percent in May one year ago.
